deck.section_name: 2. Structure & Functions in Living Organisms: Part 1
deck.title: Movement of Substances Into & Out of Cells

front_blocks.md: Define the term **diffusion**.

back_blocks.md: Diffusion is the movement of molecules from a region of **higher **concentration to a region of** lower** concentration.

cards.front_md: Define the term **diffusion**.
cards.back_md: Diffusion is the movement of molecules from a region of **higher **concentration to a region of** lower** concentration.

front_blocks.md: What is a **concentration gradient**?

back_blocks.md: A concentration gradient is the **difference in concentration** between two regions.

cards.front_md: What is a **concentration gradient**?
cards.back_md: A concentration gradient is the **difference in concentration** between two regions.

front_blocks.md: What is the result of the** random movement** of molecules during diffusion?

back_blocks.md: The result of the random movement of molecules during diffusion is that molecules **spread out** until their concentration throughout the available space is **even**; this is the point of **equilibrium**.

cards.front_md: What is the result of the** random movement** of molecules during diffusion?
cards.back_md: The result of the random movement of molecules during diffusion is that molecules **spread out** until their concentration throughout the available space is **even**; this is the point of **equilibrium**.

front_blocks.md: Define the term** osmosis.**

back_blocks.md: Osmosis is the movement of **water** molecules from a region of **higher water concentration** (dilute solution) to a region of **lower water concentration **(solution with a high solute concentration), through a **partially permeable membrane**.

cards.front_md: Define the term** osmosis.**
cards.back_md: Osmosis is the movement of **water** molecules from a region of **higher water concentration** (dilute solution) to a region of **lower water concentration **(solution with a high solute concentration), through a **partially permeable membrane**.

front_blocks.md: What type of concentration difference leads to **osmosis**?

back_blocks.md: The type of concentration difference that leads to osmosis is a difference in **water concentration **between two regions. This can also be referred to as water potential.

cards.front_md: What type of concentration difference leads to **osmosis**?
cards.back_md: The type of concentration difference that leads to osmosis is a difference in **water concentration **between two regions. This can also be referred to as water potential.

front_blocks.md: What happens to an animal cell placed in a **concentrated sugar solution**?

back_blocks.md: If an animal cell is placed into a strong sugar solution (with a lower water concentration than the cell) it will** lose water by osmosis **and will shrivel up.

cards.front_md: What happens to an animal cell placed in a **concentrated sugar solution**?
cards.back_md: If an animal cell is placed into a strong sugar solution (with a lower water concentration than the cell) it will** lose water by osmosis **and will shrivel up.

front_blocks.md: What happens when a plant cell is placed in **distilled water**?

back_blocks.md: A plant cell placed in distilled water will **gain water by osmosis**; the vacuole gets bigger, pushing the cell membrane against the cell wall, and the plant cell is described as being turgid.

cards.front_md: What happens when a plant cell is placed in **distilled water**?
cards.back_md: A plant cell placed in distilled water will **gain water by osmosis**; the vacuole gets bigger, pushing the cell membrane against the cell wall, and the plant cell is described as being turgid.

front_blocks.md: **True or False?**
Plant cells can burst due to osmosis.

back_blocks.md: **False.**
Plant cells have a supporting cell wall that prevents them from bursting due to osmosis.

cards.front_md:

cards.back_md:

front_blocks.md: Define the term **active transport**.

back_blocks.md: Active transport is the movement of particles through a cell membrane from a region of** lower concentration** to a region of **higher concentration**; this requires **energy**.

cards.front_md: Define the term **active transport**.
cards.back_md: Active transport is the movement of particles through a cell membrane from a region of** lower concentration** to a region of **higher concentration**; this requires **energy**.

front_blocks.md: **True or False?**
Active transport is the movement of particles down a concentration gradient.

back_blocks.md: **False.**
Active transport moves particles **against a concentration gradient**.

cards.front_md:
**True or False?**

Active transport is the movement of particles down a concentration gradient.
cards.back_md:
**False.**

Active transport moves particles **against a concentration gradient**.

front_blocks.md: Which cellular process **releases** **energy** for active transport?

back_blocks.md: Energy for active transport is released during the cellular process of **respiration**.

cards.front_md: Which cellular process **releases** **energy** for active transport?
cards.back_md: Energy for active transport is released during the cellular process of **respiration**.

front_blocks.md: **True or False?**
Active transport involves **carrier proteins** in the cell membrane.

back_blocks.md: **True.**
Molecules move across the cell membrane via specialised membrane **carrier proteins** during active transport.

cards.front_md:
**True or False?**

front_blocks.md: Define the phrase **surface area to volume ratio**.

back_blocks.md: Surface area to volume ratio is the** surface area** of an object** in relation to its volume**.

cards.front_md: Define the phrase **surface area to volume ratio**.
cards.back_md: Surface area to volume ratio is the** surface area** of an object** in relation to its volume**.

front_blocks.md: What happens to the surface area to volume ratio as **cell size increases**?

back_blocks.md: As cell size increases the surface area to volume ratio **decreases**.

cards.front_md: What happens to the surface area to volume ratio as **cell size increases**?
cards.back_md: As cell size increases the surface area to volume ratio **decreases**.

front_blocks.md: **True or False?**
Root hair cells have a high surface area to volume ratio.

back_blocks.md: **True.**
Root hair cells have a **large surface area** in relation to their volume; this increases the rate at which they can absorb water and minerals from the soil.

cards.front_md:

front_blocks.md: Define **diffusion distance**

back_blocks.md: Diffusion distance is the **distance** molecules have to travel when they **diffuse** from one region to another.

cards.front_md: Define **diffusion distance**
cards.back_md: Diffusion distance is the **distance** molecules have to travel when they **diffuse** from one region to another.

front_blocks.md: What is the effect of **decreasing diffusion distance** on the rate of diffusion?

back_blocks.md: As diffusion distance decreases, the rate of diffusion **increases**.

cards.front_md: What is the effect of **decreasing diffusion distance** on the rate of diffusion?
cards.back_md: As diffusion distance decreases, the rate of diffusion **increases**.

front_blocks.md: **True or False?**
Increasing temperature decreases the rate of diffusion.

back_blocks.md: **False.**
As temperature increases, the rate of diffusion also **increases**. Molecules move around faster at higher temperatures, resulting in faster diffusion.

cards.front_md:
**True or False?**

Increasing temperature decreases the rate of diffusion.
cards.back_md:
**False.**

As temperature increases, the rate of diffusion also **increases**. Molecules move around faster at higher temperatures, resulting in faster diffusion.

front_blocks.md: What is the effect of **increasing temperature** on the movement of particles?

back_blocks.md: At higher temperatures particles move around **faster**; this is because they have more** kinetic energy**.

cards.front_md: What is the effect of **increasing temperature** on the movement of particles?

front_blocks.md: **True or False?**
The rate at which red pigment leaks out of damaged beetroot cells indicates the rate of diffusion.

back_blocks.md: **True.**
The red pigment in beetroot cells can leak out when the beetroot cell membranes are damaged. The rate at which this occurs is the **diffusion rate**.

cards.front_md:
**True or False?**

The rate at which red pigment leaks out of damaged beetroot cells indicates the rate of diffusion.
cards.back_md:
**True.**

The red pigment in beetroot cells can leak out when the beetroot cell membranes are damaged. The rate at which this occurs is the **diffusion rate**.

front_blocks.md: Why is it important that all pieces of beetroot have the same** surface area** when measuring the effect of temperature on diffusion in beetroot?

back_blocks.md: Surface area **affects diffusion rate**, so differences in the surface area of the beetroot pieces would affect the results. This means that the investigation would not be measuring the effects of **temperature alone** on diffusion.

cards.front_md: Why is it important that all pieces of beetroot have the same** surface area** when measuring the effect of temperature on diffusion in beetroot?

front_blocks.md: Why does red pigment leak out of damaged beetroot cells faster at **higher temperatures**?

back_blocks.md: Red pigment leaks out of beetroot cells faster at higher temperatures because **increasing temperature increases the rate of diffusion**. This is due to increased kinetic energy of the pigment molecules.

front_blocks.md: What is the **independent variable** in the practical that investigates osmosis using potato cylinders?

back_blocks.md: The independent variable in the osmosis and potato practical is the **solute concentration** of the solution in which the potato cylinders are placed.

front_blocks.md: In the osmosis and potato practical, why is it important to **dry the potato cylinders** before weighing?

back_blocks.md: The potato cylinders are blotted with paper towels before weighing to remove any surface water that could **affect the mass** measurement.

front_blocks.md: **True or False?**
Potato cylinders placed in distilled water should gain mass due to osmosis.

back_blocks.md: **True.**

Potato cylinders placed in distilled water will gain mass due to the movement of water **into the cells** by osmosis. This will occur because distilled water has a** higher water concentration **than potato cell cytoplasm.

front_blocks.md: Give one example of a **control variable** in the osmosis and potato practical.

back_blocks.md: Examples of control variables in the osmosis and potato practical include:

- **Volume** of (e.g. sucrose) solution
- **Surface area** of potato cylinders
- Potato cylinders are all thoroughly **dried** before weighing
- Potato cylinders are left in the solutions for the same** length of time**

front_blocks.md: **True or False?**
When a potato cylinder placed in a sucrose solution does not change in mass, this indicates no overall movement of water.

back_blocks.md: **True.**
If a potato cylinder does not change mass, it means the solution it is in has the **same concentration as the cell cytoplasm**, so there is no overall movement of water by osmosis.

back_blocks.md: Repeating the experiment with multiple potato cylinders allows for the identification and exclusion of **anomalous results** when calculating the mean.
